candidate: Same baseline plus the patch-scaling production changes identified by source and artifact hashes below, before later dev integration.
mode: PR Review; sampled interactive-patch edit, persistence and GUI refresh paths.
host_cpu: Intel Core i9-13900H, 20 logical CPUs; scheduler affinity unrestricted
method: Four sequential processes in baseline/candidate/candidate/baseline order, 21 samples per process/case, pooled 42 per variant. Identical driver hash and fixtures; no warmup samples discarded. Setup, reset/undo and byte-oracle export checks are outside timings. SDK samples include Python binding overhead; worker samples include IPC. Every edit checks expected bytes; each timed worker edit is read back before undo, outside the timer. Worker SDK identity checked through /proc/<pid>/maps.
limitations: Other development builds were running on this shared host. Absolute wall times and especially tails are noisy; load averages are retained per run. No own builds or runtime tests overlapped this paired campaign.

Synthetic warm raw-x64 fixtures measure established overlays, not cold image snapshots, ELF/PE/Mach-O loading, instruction assembly, source recompilation, reanalysis, GUI paint latency, peak memory or power.
Worker commits include synchronous history and sidecar persistence; fixture projects use the local NVMe filesystem. No crash/power-loss experiment was performed by this benchmark.
Only Linux x86-64 was timed. There are no timed IDA, Binary Ninja, Ghidra or other competitor results, and these figures establish no world-ranking claim.

The optional new range API removes work proportional to patched byte payloads; output still scales with canonical row count. Durable history/sidecar snapshots and range publication still scale with total overlay state.
The 65,536-row candidate-only stress run used an earlier driver revision (its hash is retained); it proves byte-oracle correctness and records diagnostic timings, not a paired baseline speedup.

qualification.scope: Final dev-integrated delivery, separate from the controlled baseline/candidate benchmark snapshots.
qualification.limitations: Focused qualification, not a complete release certification; native Windows/macOS GUI and timing not measured locally.
qualification.pipeline_fixture_note: The existing ARM/x64 projection test now supplies the matching LowFunc entry to the current four-argument API; all original assertions are retained.
